speaker_role: unknown (narrator for CollegeVine channel, not identified as a former admissions officer)
commercial_incentive: CollegeVine is a paid admissions-consulting/platform company; video plugs its blog and services
key_insights: Frames extracurriculars as roughly 25% of the admissions decision (unsourced house figure).
Recommends a mix of breadth (a few varied activities) and depth (real leadership/commitment) rather than joining many things shallowly.
Suggests exploring broadly freshman year, then narrowing to leadership roles in 2-3 activities by senior year.

Presents a four-tier framework: Tier 1 = national-level recognition/awards; Tier 2 = state-level recognition or high leadership (e.g., club president); Tier 3 = minor leadership or regional wins; Tier 4 = general membership/regular volunteering.
Argues even Tier 4 activities (plain club membership, routine volunteering) still matter for showing who a student is, not just top-tier achievements.
Overall message: a balanced, tiered extracurricular profile helps a student stand out to admissions officers.
specific_numbers_or_facts: CollegeVine states extracurriculars make up about 25% of the admissions decision (source/methodology not given).
notable_or_distinctive: The four-tier extracurricular classification (national/state/regional/general) is a reasonably concrete mental model, though CollegeVine markets it as proprietary.
reliability_notes: Generic advice with no named admissions-officer source; the '25%' figure is asserted without evidence and the video functions partly as a lead-in to CollegeVine's paid content/blog.
